chapters.title: Designed by the land
chapters.subtitle: THE STORY OF RENAISSANCE PHUKET RESORT & SPA BEGINS WITH ITS SETTING
paragraphs: When planning for the resort began around 2006, the site at Mai Khao already presented a distinct landscape: a long beachfront setting, gentle changes in level and a lower area through the center of the property.

Rather than treating the landscape as something to be added after the architecture, it became part of the planning from the beginning. The buildings, villas, open spaces and landforms were considered together, allowing the character of the site to influence how the resort would take shape.

Guestroom buildings were positioned along the sides of the property, leaving a generous landscaped space through the center. Pool villas were grouped together in a more private setting, while the landscape between them became an important part of the guest experience.

images.alt: Aerial view of the resort, its central landscape and Mai Khao Beach

chapters.title: A story told by locals
chapters.subtitle: A WHITE TREE, A COASTAL LAND AND A WAY OF LIFE
paragraphs: In Mai Khao, local people have long spoken of a large white-barked tree that stood on a nearby hill and could be seen by passing vessls. The place was once called Mai Kaeo, the story goes, named after this distinctive tree, with the name later shiftting in local speech to Mai Khao. Its a story passed down in the community, reflecting how closely the landscape and local life have alwats been connected.

Melaleuca grows well in wet, low-lying environments and can be found in coastal areas and around peat-swamp margins in Southern Thailand. Its pale, layered bark gives the tree its distinctive appearance.
Here, the tree is more than a familiar part of the landscape. For generations, its timber and bark have been valued for their practical qualities and have supported everyday life along the coast.

chapters.title: A sequence of discovery
chapters.subtitle: THE RESORT WAS NEVER INTENDED TO REVEAL ITSELF ALL AT ONCE.
paragraphs: From the beginning, the journey through Renaissance Phuket Resort & Spa was considered as carefully as the individual spaces themselves.

Arrival begins with architecture. From the lobby and The Lounge, the view starts to open. Larger trees and denser planting frame the sides, while the centre remains more open, drawing the eye deeper into the property.

Move forward and the landscape takes over. Paths curve rather than revealing every destination directly. Water appears between planting. Pale sand begins before the beach itself. Only gradually does Mai Khao Beach become part of the view.
The original landscape concept describes this as a “sense of discovery” expressed through visual sequence—drawing guests through the resort rather than concentrating the experience in one place.
The sequence was designed to make each part of the resort lead to another:

chapters.title: The beach drawn inland
chapters.subtitle: FEEL THE COAST BEFORE YOU REACH THE SHORE
paragraphs: A broad corridor of pale sand was introduced through the central landscape, extending the character of Mai Khao Beach farther into the property.
From The Lounge, this pale opening helps draw the eye through the landscape toward the coast, while guestrooms positioned along either side look into the central space.

images.alt: Pale sand and palms extend the beach into the resort
A curved sandy pathway through tropical planting

note.title: Look closer
note.text: Notice the pale sand, the way the landscape gradually opens, and the transition to taller trees.

chapters.title: Follow the water
chapters.subtitle: WATER HAS ALWAYS BEEN PART OF THE LANDSCAPE
paragraphs: Water first appears at the lobby entrance, where the fountain introduces it as part of the arrival experience. Its placement also reflects Feng Shui, in which flowing water is associated with positive energy, prosperity and abundance, making it an auspicious element at an entrance.

From here, water becomes a recurring part of the landscape. Streams run along both sides of the guestroom buildings, following the natural fall of the land toward the centre of the property, where they meet the pond.

During the rainy season, this movement also serves a practical purpose: rainwater drains into the streams and follows the lower ground toward the pond, which occupies a naturally lower part of the site.
From the symbolic water at arrival to the streams and pond beyond, water connects the journey through the landscape.

images.alt: Curved footbridge above water and tropical planting
Water fountain at the lobby entrance

chapters.title: The spa hidden in the landscape
chapters.subtitle: FIND TRANQUILITY BEYOND THE VISIBLE
paragraphs: Quan Spa sits close to the centre of Renaissance Phuket Resort & Spa, yet it was deliberately designed to feel secluded. Raised landforms and dense tropical planting surround the spa, creating privacy and separating it from the more open spaces of the resort.

The landscape draws inspiration from Phuket’s tropical interior, where greenery, changes in elevation and water create a more enclosed environment. Here, the land rises around the spa, allowing much of the building to remain hidden from view.

Water also plays a role in the spa’s identity. The name Quan comes from a Chinese expression meaning “the source of pure water.” This connection continues inside, where the eight treatment rooms are named using words for water from different languages.
The result is a space where the landscape provides privacy, while water connects the architecture to the spa experience.

images.alt: Aerial view of Quan Spa’s circular roof surrounded by tropical landscape

chapters.quote: Eight rooms. Eight languages. One meaning: water.

chapters.title: Can you see the turtles?
chapters.subtitle: A ROOFLINE INSPIRED BY A NESTING SHORE
paragraphs: Mai Khao's association with nesting sea turtles became one of the references explored in the architecture of Renaissance Phuket Resort & Spa. Rather than reproducing the form of a turtle literally, the idea was translated more subtly through the softened roof forms and natural materiality of the villas.
It is a detail that can be easy to miss at ground level.
From a higher viewpoint, however, the relationship becomes easier to see: individual roof forms sit among the landscape rather than forming a single continuous architectural block.
It is one of the quieter examples of how something found beyond the resort's boundary influenced what was designed within it.

images.alt: Individual villa roofs nestled in greenery beside the Andaman Sea

illustration.alt: Booklet line drawing of a sea turtle

chapters.title: Rooms reimagined
chapters.subtitle: REDEFINING SOUTHERN SEASIDE FOLKWAYS
paragraphs: The renewed guestrooms and pool villas draw inspiration from Southern Thailand's coastal heritage, translating traditional craftsmanship, materials and everyday objects into contemporary interior design.

Completed in 2025, the renovation follows a concept described as “Redefining the Southern Seaside Folkways.” It draws on the practical knowledge passed through generations, where architecture and everyday objects were shaped by local materials, climate and the needs of daily life.

Rather than recreating traditional interiors, the design reinterprets familiar elements through contemporary forms and functions. Privacy screens and breathable walls, once practical features of Southern vernacular architecture, provide inspiration for details within the renewed spaces.

In the guestrooms, the design also takes cues from traditional Thai houses. Wood ceiling details reference the living spaces beneath these structures, while a palette of sand and ocean tones reflects the contrast between Mai Khao's shoreline and the Andaman Sea.

images.alt: Pool Villa bedroom with a timber ceiling and private pool beyond

images.alt: Deluxe Room bedroom with shoreline-inspired headboard
images.caption: Deluxe Room

note.title: Familiar ideas, new forms
note.text: Look for the architectural references in the screens, ceiling details and cabinetry. Each offers a contemporary interpretation of an element once shaped by everyday life.

continuation: The Pool Villas draw inspiration from Southern folk art, reinterpreting traditional fishing tools, ceramic dishes and wicker lanterns through contemporary decorative details. In the Deluxe Rooms, fishermen’s rope knots inspire wall decorations, bringing a familiar element of coastal life into the interiors and connecting the design to Mai Khao’s seaside heritage.

Pearls introduce another layer of local identity. Long associated with the Andaman coast, their rounded forms and reflective qualities are referenced through decorative lighting, while wooden screens draw inspiration from traditional Southern Thai houses. Their angled panels reinterpret breathable walls and privacy screens, allowing light and air to pass through while maintaining privacy. Together, these elements bring coastal influences and practical architectural ideas into the renewed interiors.

chapters.title: The Hydra Collection
paragraphs: Look around the lobby and discover two sculptural forms that blur the line between furniture and art. Created by artist and designer EggWong, the Hydra Collection was designed exclusively for Renaissance Phuket Resort & Spa in 2010, exploring the relationship between man and woman through contrasting yet complementary forms.
Look closer and you’ll find inspiration from the coast. Their organic shapes reference coral, cuttlebone and sea cucumber, reinterpreted through abstract forms.
Crafted from anodized aluminium, stainless steel and marble, the pieces feature a neutral palette chosen to complement the natural surroundings of Mai Khao.
